label: input u, or <DEL>/g/b/p in sequences starting with v/n/j/1/c/y/k (input/delimiter phase)
explanation: Input-driven, gated by sequence context. Fires almost only during the original phase (67% of mass) and on the <DEL> step (29%). Copy steps are near silent (4% of mass, rate 0.2x). The strongest trigger is the input token u (rate 0.33 among all u steps, 61% when u arrives before <DEL>), and u produces the top activations, most of all at t=3-4. Weaker triggers are <DEL>, g, b, p (and to a lesser degree w, 2, d, s). These depend on the first original token: rates are about 2.5x when the sequence starts with v, n, j, 1, c, y or k. It fires mostly on the first occurrence of a token (in_first=1 holds 91% of mass) and on mid-sequence positions t=2-5. Taking the trigger tokens alone gives recall of about 0.68 but precision of only 0.24. The first-token gate brings precision up to about 0.55, so a large unmodelled hidden-state dependence remains. It is weak or silent on q, j, 3 and most other letters as inputs, and during copying.
